runtime_references.command:
/bin/bash -lc "find . -name AGENTS.md -o -name pyproject.toml -o -path './openspec/*' | sed -n '1,200p'
printf '\\n--- openspec-propose ---\\n'
sed -n '1,240p' /workspace/.agents/skills/openspec-propose/SKILL.md
printf '\\n--- openspec-apply-change ---\\n'
sed -n '1,260p' /workspace/.agents/skills/openspec-apply-change/SKILL.md"

/bin/bash -lc "find . -name AGENTS.md -o -name pyproject.toml -o -path './openspec/*' | sed -n '1,200p'
printf '\\n--- openspec-propose ---\\n'
sed -n '1,240p' /workspace/.agents/skills/openspec-propose/SKILL.md
printf '\\n--- openspec-apply-change ---\\n'
sed -n '1,260p' /workspace/.agents/skills/openspec-apply-change/SKILL.md"

/bin/bash -lc "openspec list --json && openspec context --json && sed -n '1,200p' openspec/config.yaml && find src tests -maxdepth 3 -type f | grep -E '(templating|test_templating|test_basic)' | sed -n '1,120p'"

note: Artifact presence proves setup only. A non-bare treatment requires a direct raw Codex tool command that reads a project-local guidance artifact (or, for Keelson, invokes guide/ask/check/record) to establish activation. Listing paths alone is insufficient. This does not establish causal effectiveness. Any direct global instruction-path read makes a run ineligible for a clean causal comparison.
